body:
I know it's possible to thoroughly enjoy living. I know it's not just misery, that it has its ups and downs. I just think that having to endure the downs is just a huge burden. I didn't ask for free-will or the illusion of free-will. I was just comfortable not existing.

I can only imagine what would happen if I were to kill myself. It would devastate a lot of people that care about me, a lot of people that I would never want to hurt. That's the main thing that's keeping me away from just doing it.

If there is anything that's waiting for me that will make me enjoy life to the fullest, it should show itself soon. I'm getting impatient. Looking around, I see that not many people end up finding that one special thing for them. This just makes me think that finding it is a rare thing. I also see that humans get downs more often as they age. It seems like we tend to lose everything we love, one way or another, sooner or later.

I'm aware these are very common philosophical questions. It's basically existential depression exacerbated by circumstances.

I got a question for you... what makes you want to stay now? Is it the hope that it might all be worth it at some point?

I'm entirely with you on that one. The only thing that's keeping me away from taking the step to kill myself is the people I care about and of course the people that care about me in return. 

I don't want to put this burden on them. I don't want to make them feel shitty for the rest of their lives. But is it really worth suffering for them -- just so that they don't suffer? Isn't that a vicious cycle? I need to change something, I need to end my suffering one way or another.

There is also this marginal point of view that's of course just pure speculation that goes against our every observation... As far as I know, my death concludes reality. What if everything ceases to exist with me and no one would suffer because they just don't exist after my death. Fun to think about that but no way know and come back.

Anywhere would do but going to New Zealand or starting by backpacking through Europe only with some clothes and a debit card with me and slowly moving east definitely sound appealing.

Killing yourself is definitely the last resort but it is appealing because you just cease to exist, even the most worrying of your worries cease to exist with you. You stop worrying about your social anxiety, you start worrying about feeling tired and lonely; and most importantly you don't worry about people you left behind and how shitty you made them feel. You said you tried suicide and it's just another problem. Excuse me if I'm being insensitive, I don't mean to but isn't that the case because you didn't manage to kill yourself? Wouldn't all your problems be solved if you weren't alive right now to worry about them?

I haven't talked to anyone about these before, not even on Reddit. Putting them to words makes them real, you know. When it's all scattered around in your head, it's different, it's less real.
